chunks: And whatever is in it from Al-Hasan ibn Harun, I have narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan—may Allah be pleased with him—from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanti, from Abd al-Karim ibn Amr, from al-Hasan ibn Harun.

key_terms.الْبَزَنْطِيِّ: A well-known transmitter designation within the chain of narration.
key_terms.الْحَسَنِ بْنِ هَارُونَ: The final named transmitter to whom this chain leads.
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I transmitted it; indicates direct attribution of the report through a stated chain.
key_terms.عَبْدِ الْكَرِيمِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو: A named narrator appearing in this transmission path.
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ الصَّفَّارِ: A key transmitter in the sanad/isnad cited here.

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain to al-Hasan ibn Harun in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage clarifies the sanad/isnad through which the author transmits reports from al-Hasan ibn Harun in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih. Its significance lies in documenting the precise chain of transmission for hadith authentication and source attribution.
